thread:
asha: Heads-up — saw a customer report where a streaming request retried and the toolcall side-effect tokens got double-counted in billing. attaching logs in a sec.
brad: ouch. is this the streaming -> toolcall -> truncated response flow?
sylvie: yup. pattern is: client starts stream, runtime invokes toolcall, tool returns, but the stream later gets a truncated chunk and client retries the whole request. we end up emitting two toolcall-charge events. :facepalm:
asha: exact log snippet: 
```
# runtime log
[2024-04-10T12:03:15Z] request=R42 stream_id=S-9 state=streaming toolcall_id=T-77 charge_emitted=false
[2024-04-10T12:03:16Z] request=R42 toolcall=T-77 result=200 tokens=120 charge_emitted=true
[2024-04-10T12:03:16Z] billing-bot: ChargeEvent(toolcall=T-77 tokens=120)
[2024-04-10T12:03:18Z] request=R42 stream_truncation=partial retry_allowed=true
[2024-04-10T12:03:19Z] request=R42 retry=start new_req=R43
[2024-04-10T12:03:19Z] request=R43 toolcall=T-77 (replayed) tokens=120 charge_emitted=true
[2024-04-10T12:03:19Z] billing-bot: ChargeEvent(toolcall=T-77 tokens=120)
```
brad: interesting — toolcall id got replayed so the runtime couldn't tell this was the same side-effect. we need stronger idempotency or a different billing anchor.
michael: two angles: 1) dedupe at billing layer by toolcall id + request parent, 2) only emit a charge when final delivery to client confirmed (but that breaks near-real-time billing/streaming metrics).
sylvie: we already try to avoid delaying charge emit because consoles rely on near-real-time token breakdown for dashboards and SLAs. delaying would cause a noisy UX.
asha: another idea: mark toolcall charges with a provisional flag and emit a finalization event when request completes (SUCCESS/FAILED/REPLAYED). billing pipeline dedupes provisional charges if finalization says REPLAYED. that keeps near-realtime counts but allows correction.
brad: how do we detect REPLAYED vs genuinely retried distinct toolcalls? current toolcall ids are generated per invocation by the runtime; if the client retry replays the same upstream call we currently generate a new id. we could plumb an idempotency token from request => toolcall. e.g., `X-Runtime-Toolcall-Anchor: <sha>` so replayed runs reuse anchor.
sylvie: plumbing idempotency tokens through various async queues is doable but brittle. also we have cases where toolcalls are non-idempotent intentionally (e.g., payment capture). we must never silently dedupe those.
michael: agree. we need an explicit signal from the model-serving surface: `toolcall_is_idempotent=true|false` and an `idempotency_key` header; only dedupe when both indicate safe. default should be conservative (non-idempotent).
asha: console UX question: if we mark provisional charges then later revoke, dashboards need to show corrections and not confuse customers. we already have 'corrections' rows for batch billing — can console show a negative adjustment line with ?reason=stream-retry-dedupe?
brad: yes, but we should surface an explanation and link to a docs page. also rate limits/quota checks shouldn't let a provisional charge allow exceeding quota. i.e., provisional shouldn't count against hard quota until finalized. quotas should use committed charges only.
sylvie: that is a good separation: console/metrics show provisional for visibility; quota enforcement uses committed. avoids exploit where someone streams to eat provisional spots.
michael: operationally, implement plan: 
1) runtime adds idempotency_key on toolcall when it can detect replay intent (propagated from client or derived from request hash). default blank.
2) charge emitter writes ChargeEvent with `status=provisional|committed` and `idempotency_key` + `toolcall_signature`.
3) when request terminal state known, emitter writes ChargeFinalization(toolcall_sig, final_status=committed|revoked) which billing dedupes/adjusts.
4) console shows provisional with a subtle badge and shows final adjustments.

code idea: 
```
headers = {"X-Toolcall-Idempotency": "sha256(req_id + prompt_prefix)", "X-Toolcall-Idempotent": "true"}
# runtime ensures same header is used on retries
```

billing-bot: I can emit adjustment events automatically if ChargeFinalization indicates revoke. sample adjustment: `Adjustment(toolcall=T-77 delta=-120 reason=stream-retry-dedupe)`
asha: nice. what about edge: streaming partial tokens already billed (model output tokens) vs toolcall tokens? we have asymmetry: model output tokens can be streamed per-chunk and we already have partial token accounting. toolcall is a separate billing dimension. must ensure adjustment doesn't leave model tokens charged and toolcall not, producing mismatch for customer reconciliation.
brad: agreed — we should tie adjustments so that finalization is atomic across token categories for a request: model_output_tokens + toolcall_tokens adjusted together. billing pipeline can support atomic adjustments by referencing request_id.
sylvie: one more gotcha: what if the replay goes to a different region/route and ends up invoking a different tool endpoint? idempotency_key must be globally resolvable or carried in the request payload so the tool server can dedupe. that's an ops rollout challenge.
michael: rollout strategy: start with purely runtime-local dedupe and provisional/commit events; do not auto-dedupe at tool backend until we have a routed header propagation pattern. phase 1 buys us correction capability without breaking semantics.
asha: ok action items: 
- brad: sketch proto for ChargeEvent+ChargeFinalization and provisional flag (this week)
- sylvie: audit places where we generate toolcall ids and add idempotency propagation points (next 2 sprints)
- michael: console mock for provisional badges + adjustment rows (next sprint)
- billing-bot: add test pipeline to simulate replay + finalization (I'll open a ticket).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: `runtime/charge-emitter v0.18.3` -> staging at 2024-04-11T03:00:00Z
brad: thanks. also add a small unit test: simulate stream truncation -> retry loop and assert billing emits provisional + finalization and net charge = 1x.
sylvie: will do.
asha: awesome — let's keep notes in a short RFC, call it `rfc/billing-toolcall-provisional.md` and cc @product and @support for customer impact.
michael: I'll draft the RFC after the proto.
asha: thanks all.
